title: RT5: a mutation tool that fails to reload must return partial/failure with post-reload diagnostics
summary: A mutation tool whose post-write reload fails reports success rather than a partial/failure result carrying the post-reload diagnostics (v0.6.7 measurement).
notes: Source: emilyriehl/Codex-Homotopy-Group agda-mcp-ux-report/README.md spec RT5 (v0.6.7 measurement). affectedTool is best-inferred (mutation-tool family) - confirm the exact tool during re-verification. Re-verified 2026-07-04 (run-id rt5-20260703) through dogfood-run/dogfood-wrapup against current main: CONFIRMED -- agda_apply_edit (the deterministic mutation-tool probe used; a give's own accept path requires the expr to already type-check, so it cannot independently produce this shape) wrote an ill-typed replacement (myZero = definitelyNotInScopeXyz) and returned top-level ok:true/classification:'ok'/data.applied:true, while data.text's embedded prose reads 'Reloaded with errors: 0 goal(s) remaining' plus the raw NotInScope error and the misleading 'Goal diff: solved ?0, ?1, ?2' -- no structured field anywhere distinguishes this from a genuine success. defectKind corrected from wrong-result to false-green to match this queue's own established usage for an ok:true response wrapping a real failure (see bfcba437f5426fd6/5abecc959e43fef3, the identical shape). Root cause is shared with those two entries: registerTextTool/registerGoalTextTool (src/tools/tool-registration.ts) unconditionally wrap a non-throwing callback in okEnvelope, and reloadAndDiagnose (src/session/reload-and-diagnose.ts) reports a reload failure only as prose text, never a structured field -- confirmed to affect every write-capable proof tool (case_split/give/refine/refine_exact/intro/auto/apply_edit) identically by source inspection. title: RT6: agda_load must distinguish visible goals/hidden metas/constraints/source holes/file-completeness
summary: agda_load's response conflates these five states into one signal; the no-goals-but-constraints-hold-an-error sub-case is the same labeling issue tracked by the agda_proof_status entry (see relatedFingerprint).
notes: Source: emilyriehl/Codex-Homotopy-Group agda-mcp-ux-report/README.md spec RT6 (v0.6.7 measurement). Cross-references the agda_proof_status mislabeling entry for its sub-case; the broader five-state-conflation ask remains its own tracked item. Re-verified 2026-07-04 (run-id rt6-20260703) through dogfood-run/dogfood-wrapup against current main: CONFIRMED as missing-feature. Of the five asked-for distinctions (visible goals, hidden metas, constraints, source hole syntax, file completeness), agda_load's response schema (loadDataSchema) exposes visible goals (goalCount/goalIds) and hidden metas (invisibleGoalCount) directly, and file completeness via isComplete/classification -- but TWO remain conflated: (1) source hole syntax has no field of its own; classifyLoadResult() (src/agda/session-load-helpers.ts) folds a text-scanned sourceHoleCount into the single derived boolean hasHoles, with no way for a client to see the count or distinguish it from a protocol-reported goal. Live probe on MixedGoalsErrors.agda (one valid {!!} hole plus one unrelated hard type error later in the file) reproduced finding #4's exact historical symptom LIVE: the response reports goalCount:0, invisibleGoalCount:0, hasHoles:false, classification:'type-error' -- the file's own genuinely-present, syntactically-valid hole is completely invisible to the client, because runLoad's needsExplicitHoleScan gate (src/agda/session-load-impl.ts) only runs countExplicitSourceHoles when parsed.success is true, so a hole co-occurring with an unrelated hard error is never scanned for at all. (2) constraints has no field on agda_load's own response schema whatsoever -- it exists only on a different tool, agda_proof_status (cross-referenced via fdc90bfde12fb938, not double-counted here per the plan's instruction). Second fixture (MixedVisibleInvisible.agda) confirms goalCount/invisibleGoalCount work correctly for the visible/hidden-metas distinction when Agda's own protocol actually reports both goals as visible (both do, on Agda 2.8.0 -- see the fixture's own comment). ADDITIONAL FINDING (oracle-tooling, not this spec): dogfood-wrapup auto-filed this session's MixedGoalsErrors.agda capture as fingerprint 1220f2840142aab8 (an ORCL-01 server-false-green-candidate on the SAME hasHoles field) -- root-cause analysis (see that entry's own notes) shows this stems from scripts/oracle/orcl-01-differential.mjs's runColdLoadAndDiff calling countExplicitSourceHoles UNCONDITIONALLY, unlike the live server's own needsExplicitHoleScan gate, i.e. a fidelity gap in the ORACLE's cold-replay reimplementation, not an independent live-server defect beyond what is already recorded here. The plausible fix for THIS entry (RT6 itself) is the UX report's 'Suggested Schema Direction' response-schema rework -- a deferred-ideas re-triage candidate (D-10); the disposition (fix vs re-triage) belongs to plan 06-06, not here. Full envelopes in .planning/research/RT-REVERIFY.md. DEFERRED (Phase 6): the remaining gap (source hole syntax has no field of its own; constraints absent from agda_load's schema entirely) is the UX report's own "Suggested Schema Direction" response-schema rework — the pre-approved deferral class for RT6-style five-state asks (named explicitly in this plan's own objective). A structural rework of agda_load's response schema is out of D-10's per-entry <=2-src-file fix appetite and belongs to a dedicated future plan. Remains triaged for a later milestone's queue review. Cross-referenced auto-filed entry 1220f2840142aab8 (a fidelity gap in the ORACLE tooling itself, not a second independent client-facing defect) is dispositioned separately below.

title: RT7: a timeout must identify whether Agda exited, is still running, or produced no protocol response
summary: On a command timeout, the response does not distinguish whether the underlying Agda process exited, is still running, or simply produced no protocol response in the window (v0.6.7 measurement).
notes: Source: emilyriehl/Codex-Homotopy-Group agda-mcp-ux-report/README.md spec RT7 (v0.6.7 measurement). affectedTool is best-inferred (most timeout-prone command family) - confirm the exact tool during re-verification. Re-verified 2026-07-04 (run-id rt7-20260703) through dogfood-run/dogfood-wrapup against current main with AGDA_MCP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS=300 (the driver-env fault-injection lever, set only on the one-off shell invocation, never exported globally): CONFIRMED -- agda_load timed out after receiving 15 real protocol responses (Status x2, HighlightingInfo x8, RunningInfo, ClearRunningInfo, ClearHighlighting, DisplayInfo, and a terminal InteractionPoints), with the last response only 96ms before the 300ms deadline -- i.e. Agda was demonstrably alive and actively mid-flight, not crashed and not failed to start. The surfaced envelope is ok:false/classification:'process-error' with diagnostics[0].nextAction verbatim: 'The Agda subprocess crashed or could not be started. Run agda --version to confirm it is installed and on PATH (or set AGDA_BIN), then retry the load.' -- a specific, wrong causal claim directly contradicted by the response's own responseCount/responseKinds evidence. Root cause: processErrorResult() (src/session/load-tool-shared.ts) hardcodes this crash/startup nextAction text for EVERY session.load() throw, including the timeout Error thrown by AgdaTransport.sendCommand (src/session/agda-transport.ts), which itself already terminates the Agda process on timeout (terminateAgdaProcess(proc)) -- a fact never communicated to the caller either. classification 'process-error' cannot distinguish 'timed out while alive' from 'crashed on its own' from 'never started' from 'produced no protocol response at all' -- all four collapse to one classification and one (misleading, in the timed-out-while-alive case) diagnostic. This is byte-for-byte the same shape CHG's finding #6 recorded in v0.6.7 (still alive on current main, same wrong nextAction framing, just now surfaced via the generic process-error path rather than whatever v0.6.7 called it). dogfood-wrapup correctly skipped the oracle triad for this capture (orcl01=skip: a failed/process-error load leaves no load-family completeness tuple to diff), 0 filed -- the pipeline pass itself is documented in .agda-mcp/runs/rt7-20260703/wrapup-report.json even though nothing was auto-filed, satisfying D-06. wrapup was re-run with AGDA_MCP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS unset (normal env) per T-06-09's mitigation, so the low-timeout lever never leaked into the oracle's own probes. Full envelope in .planning/research/RT-REVERIFY.md. DEFERRED (Phase 6): distinguishing timed-out-while-alive from crashed from never-started from produced-no-protocol-response requires a dedicated timeout/processState taxonomy fed from the responseCount/sawStatusDone/lastResponseKind evidence AgdaTransport already collects, threaded through processErrorResult()'s single hardcoded nextAction across every session.load()-family throw site — the pre-approved timeout-state-taxonomy deferral class for RT7-style asks (named explicitly in this plan's own objective). This is a diagnostic-taxonomy design decision, not a mechanical <=2-src-file fix. Remains triaged for a later milestone's queue review.

title: RT8: a stale reload must report the previous+new classification together with the reason
summary: Same family as the re-verified flagship transitive-staleness false-green (see relatedFingerprint): re-verify whether agda_load_no_metas and related tools in this family still lack a combined previous+new classification report.
notes: Source: emilyriehl/Codex-Homotopy-Group agda-mcp-ux-report/README.md spec RT8. In one session: (1) agda_load_no_metas on clean Main.agda -> ok-complete, reloaded:false, staleBeforeLoad:false (correct, a genuine first load); (2) out-of-band overwrite of Dep.agda with Dep.broken.agda's content (raw writeFileSync, mirrors CHG-REVERIFY's convention); (3) agda_load_no_metas on Main.agda again -> type-error (UnequalTerms, Bool !=< Nat) -- STILL reloaded:false, staleBeforeLoad:false (now factually wrong: this genuinely is a reload of an already-loaded file) and NO previousClassification field anywhere in data, and no regression-style diagnostic of any kind. Root cause confirmed by source inspection: registerAgdaLoadNoMetas (src/session/register-agda-load-no-metas.ts) hardcodes reloaded:false/staleBeforeLoad:false unconditionally and never reads session.getLastClassification()/getLastLoadedAt() at all, unlike agda_load's own registration -- this is a 100% deterministic gap, not a timing-dependent one. It may have been modified since, or a dependency may have changed.' Full envelopes in .planning/research/RT-REVERIFY.md. FIXED (Phase 6 wave 4, plan 06-06): registerAgdaLoadNoMetas now mirrors agda_load's own session-history read (previousClassification/previousLoadedAtMs/reloaded/staleBeforeLoad, plus the session-regression diagnostic on a success -> failure transition) instead of hardcoding reloaded:false/staleBeforeLoad:false. Report-side change only, no new session-state tracking (loadDataSchema already carried these optional fields since agda_load populates them today). title: dogfood-run.mjs never writes run-report.json when the proxy process is hard-killed, blocking every Codex-driven run from entering the loop
summary: finalize() in scripts/dogfood/dogfood-run.mjs writes run-report.json ONLY on child-close/child-error/agent-stdin-close, and the proxy registers no SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP handlers. Codex hard-kills the MCP server process it directly manages (the dogfood-run.mjs proxy itself) on both interactive quit and `codex exec` completion, triggering none of those three events. Empirically observed during 07-06's E2E-01 live acceptance session (2026-07-04): 8 run directories under .agda-mcp/runs/2026-07-04T14-*Z-* all contain transcript.jsonl but NONE contain run-report.json, including the one fully successful interactive proving session (2026-07-04T14-47-00-924Z-442e77f2, 8 tool calls: agda_load -> agda_goal_type -> agda_case_split x2 -> agda_goal_catalog -> agda_give -> agda_typecheck -> agda_proof_status). Per dogfood-wrapup.mjs's own design (scriptMain's existsSync(reportPath) gate), a run with no run-report.json is refused outright ('no run report found ... has this run id been recorded by dogfood-run.mjs?'), so no Codex-driven dogfooding run — successful or not — can enter the fix-queue loop.
notes: Root-caused during 07-06 (E2E-01 live acceptance) continuation, not surfaced by the oracle triad (this is a defect in the dogfooding ORCHESTRATOR script itself, not in the live agda-mcp-server response the oracle triad judges) -- hence capturePath/verdictPath null, matching this queue's own established precedent for hand-authored, source-inspection-derived entries (see e.g. eb7439cb3ed9d6b9, fdc90bfde12fb938). Evidence: 8 run dirs from 2026-07-04 (2026-07-04T14-40-06-340Z-2c6eb697, 14-44-01-557Z-16ad5c5a, 14-44-12-669Z-19efe349, 14-44-30-276Z-607ab8f7, 14-45-11-014Z-a4f2652a, 14-47-00-924Z-442e77f2, 14-55-28-507Z-de11e5d0, 14-59-39-259Z-93b432eb) each have transcript.jsonl and zero run-report.json. Codex version: codex-cli 0.142.5. Design citation: dogfood-run.mjs's own header comment (~line 171, the EPIPE-guard rationale) states verbatim: 'no run-report.json means dogfood-wrapup refuses the run and every staged capture goes unjudged' -- i.e. the script's own author already anticipated this failure mode for one narrower trigger (an EPIPE on a dead agent's stdout) but the fix at that time did not cover the broader case of the PROXY's OWN process being killed before finalize() ever runs. SECONDARY, DOCUMENTED-NOT-FIXED, Codex-side defect (do not fix here, context only): `codex exec` (codex-cli 0.142.5) cancels every MCP tool call after the first ('user cancelled MCP tool call', observed directly in the operator's terminal during this session), while interactive Codex is unaffected -- corroborated by the transcripts themselves: every codex-exec-driven run this session recorded 0-3 tool calls total (14-45-11: 1x agda_load; 14-55-28: 3x agda_load; 14-59-39: 2x agda_load; the three 14-44-* probes: 0 tool calls), never completing a multi-step proof, versus the one interactive session (14-47-00) which completed the full 8-call flow cleanly. This defect is being fixed in-place (see status transitions below): incremental report checkpointing (write run-report.json after every recorded action, marked finalized:false, so an uncatchable SIGKILL at any point still leaves a trustworthy on-disk record) plus SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP handlers for the catchable path, plus dogfood-wrapup.mjs accepting a finalized:false report with a loud warning instead of silently treating it as a complete run. TRIAGED: deterministically reproduced via a from-RED regression suite (test/unit/tools/dogfood-run-report-checkpoint.test.ts), confirmed RED against pre-fix code -- all 3 tests failed with 'waitFor: predicate never became true' (no run-report.json ever appears, neither at startup nor after a recorded tool call, and finalize() never fires on a hard SIGKILL) -- before any fix code was written.
